scope: Formal fresh-process cost comparison of the frozen generated-JS A0 frontend against C/Wasm, historical Canonical/Dense and the current flat TypeScript research reader. Six actual application/compiler inputs, one discarded warmup and seven rotated measured rounds. No production frontend, grammar, public routing, emitter, runtime or default was changed.

decision.reason: On this Linux/Node runtime and all six frozen inputs, generated JS has higher median frontend, pipeline and fresh-child wall time and higher frontend RSS than every control. Its smaller arena-only Wasm memory excludes its JavaScript heap/JIT/code/GC and does not establish lower total memory. Existing production defaults remain unchanged.

protocol.coldParentPreparation: Fresh TypeScript builds in all three clean checkouts; strict cold JS re-emission, generic arena reproduction and complete strict native C/Wasm reproduction before samples. Exact shared compiler/source/configuration/toolchain inputs and structural API signatures checked by the frozen harness.
protocol.rotation: For each round -1 through 6 and input id, rotate five arms by (round+1+id+index)%5. Every cell runs in a fresh process. Warmup cells remain archived and are excluded from medians.
protocol.outputControl: Every cell emits byte-identical C through one historical emitter. Frozen historical output hashes permit only the recorded first-line compiler-version banner substitution; the controller verifies the substituted frozen hash before samples.
protocol.scope: Frozen flattened whole-program inputs, old Canonical/Dense controls, current flat TS control and compiled A0 frontend. Parser/checker plus one historical C text emitter. Frontend instantiation/upload/typed-IR decoding included. Graph I/O, shipping CLI startup, formatter, model inference and generated-target execution excluded. Every fresh process preloads the common candidate SDK and its selected artifact; candidate artifact also preloaded for historical and TS controls. Per-sample preload records identify every component, hash and size, separating JavaScript text from Wasm bytes. Artifact validation and module compilation are outside frontend/pipeline phases; fresh-child wall time includes process startup, preparation and final proof checks. No official source cutover or no-regression conclusion is implied.
protocol.detail: Reuse the archived frontend experiment input corpus and rotated fresh-process protocol; one discarded warmup round and seven measured rounds. Every arm uses the historical baseline C text emitter, so frontend IR is compared through one fixed backend even when frontend artifact code generation changes. Every emitted C hash must match the baseline control. That control must match the frozen reference after the explicitly recorded compiler-version banner substitution. JS compiled-backend mode requires a cold parent re-emission with exact compiler outputs/configuration and SDK/source inventory, the same raw and normalized A0 closure/count and eight structural API signatures, identical common compiler implementation/configuration, explicit host-word IO and optimization, same arena/libc/builtins/toolchain, exact generic-arena rebuild and strict C native rebuild. A hashed immutable parent proof binds every worker to the actual component and SDK bytes; compiler rebuilding never occurs per worker. JavaScript text bytes are distinct from arena Wasm bytes. Module preparation includes artifact/SDK validation plus fresh ESM import and Wasm module compilation outside frontendMs, and remains inside child wall. First-call JS lazy JIT is included in frontendMs. No same-process warm cohort or total engine-memory equivalence is claimed.
protocol.memoryMethod: Live frontend RSS/heap/external/arrayBuffer memory captured before emission. Module preparation and pre-preparation memory are separately recorded; process/SDK import startup remains in child wall. Initial peak/live RSS exposes any inherited launch or preload floor; maxRSS alone cannot establish small-cell frontend parity. JS engine code/JIT/GC cannot be isolated by these process counters. wasmLinearMemoryBytes includes only retained Wasm buffers (arena-only for JS), not JS heap/code/JIT/GC; no cross-engine total-memory equivalence is implied.

quietWindow.coordinator: Root cleared the quiet window after all other local builders/test runners stopped; other agents held builds and tests until controller success and final proof verification.

artifacts.scope: Component bytes only. These are not complete bootstrap package sizes, installed SDK sizes, execution binary sizes or total engine-memory measurements.

comparisonRecord.policy: Every higher, lower and equal observation is retained with exact absolute and relative differences. No tolerance, significance filter, load excuse or successful subset suppresses a measured loss. Ratios against zero are null.

archive.inspectionOnly: Proof/build snapshots replace local paths with named placeholders; original raw byte lengths and SHA-256 digests remain in snapshot-manifest.json. All 240 timing sample bytes and all six prepared source input bytes are preserved exactly. The analysis recipe is an inspection copy with named path placeholders. Executable proof files are rebuilt through the strict frozen harness in clean replay checkouts.

replay.instructions: Recover the exact frozen candidate source bundle and its prerequisite, create separate clean candidate, C control and historical checkouts, install dependencies and use the recorded matching native toolchain. Rebuild the normal direct/JS and explicit disabled-diagnostics C artifacts. Run the unchanged normal --cross-backend command from cost-preparation.md into a fresh output directory after a new quiet-window clearance. The archived command uses named path placeholders. The parent regenerates executable worker proofs rather than reusing inspection snapshots.

limitations: This is the cold fresh-process cohort on the recorded Linux/x64 Node/V8 runtime. Persistent/warmed frontend sessions, browsers and other engines remain unmeasured.

The phases include parse/check/typed-IR decoding and one fixed historical C emitter. Graph disk I/O, shipping CLI startup, formatter, AI inference/edit success and execution of generated application targets are outside this cohort.

All historical/TypeScript controls preload the candidate artifact and common SDK as required by the frozen research harness; C control uses its C artifact. Child wall describes this instrumented experiment, not shipping CLI startup.

RSS and heap counters retain import/preparation floors and allocator/GC effects. Arena-only Wasm memory does not isolate JS JIT/code/GC or total process cost. No forced GC or engine-memory equivalence claim is used.
These experimental losses justify retaining current defaults. They do not complete the universal syntax cutover or any full repository/platform release gate.
